title: PMLBmini: A Tabular Classification Benchmark Suite for Data-Scarce Applications
summary: Tabular benchmarks are not geared toward data-scarce applications, making empirical comparisons on small datasets difficult to interpret. The paper introduces PMLBmini, 44 binary classification datasets with sample sizes at most 500 selected from PMLB, and evaluates AutoML frameworks, off-the-shelf tabular deep networks, and L2-regularized logistic regression with stratified 3-fold cross-validation. Logistic regression lies within 3% of the best AutoML or deep learning method on 55% of datasets, while AutoML tends to help on more complex datasets and deep models on feature distributions resembling their meta-training data.

match_target.why: It is the user-specified target and the cheapest reproduction: one 32-sample dataset and a 3-fold logistic-regression run. Although it is a single-dataset baseline value, it directly verifies the reported LR number used in the low-data comparison.

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUC is a bounded score and the paper prints 0.17 in [0,1]; parity5 has only 32 samples, far below 2,000, so use 0.02 absolute (two AUC points). No repeated-run standard deviation is reported.

requirements.stmt: Build PMLBmini from all binary classification datasets with sample sizes ≤500 in PMLB, yielding 44 datasets.
requirements.quote: We selected all binary classification datasets with sample sizes ≤500 from the curated benchmark suite with the largest number of small-sized datasets, PMLB

requirements.stmt: Shuffle each dataset and encode original labels to {0,1} before method-specific preprocessing.
requirements.quote: We shuffled all datasets and encoded all labels to {0, 1}.

requirements.stmt: Use an L2-regularized logistic regression designed to be deterministic, matching the paper's conic formulation or an equivalent fixed solver.
requirements.quote: We use a continuous conic formulation that is designed to be run-to-run deterministic (MOSEK ApS, 2023)

requirements.stmt: For logistic regression, re-encode labels to {-1,1} and min-max scale all features.
requirements.quote: We re-encode all labels to {-1, 1} and ”min-max” scale all features for logistic regression.

requirements.stmt: Tune λ over the fixed grid [0.5,0.1,0.02,0.004] using deviance as the validation score.
requirements.quote: using [0.5, 0.1, 0.02, 0.004] as the hyperparameter grid and the deviance as the validation score.

requirements.stmt: Evaluate discriminative performance with the area under the ROC curve (AUC).
requirements.quote: we evaluate estimators with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC)

requirements.stmt: Use a stratified 3-fold cross-validation to obtain mean test performance.
requirements.quote: using a stratified, 3-fold cross validation procedure to obtain mean test performances

requirements.stmt: Apply the 3h mean-test-AUC budget as 1h per fold for non-LR methods.
requirements.quote: the mean test AUC with a 3h runtime limit via a stratified, 3-fold cross-validation procedure (i.e., 1h per fold)

requirements.stmt: Track the best λ* on the whole data for reporting in Table 3.
requirements.quote: For logistic regression, we also tracked the best L2-regularization hyperparameter value λ∗obtained on the whole data

requirements.stmt: Use nested cross-validation for logistic-regression test AUC, not non-nested CV.
requirements.quote: used a nested instead of a non-nested cross-validation procedure

requirements.stmt: Run AutoPrognosis 0.1.21 with default settings from Python 3.10.13.
requirements.quote: AutoPrognosis 0.1.21 was run from Python 3.10.13 with the default settings

requirements.stmt: Run AutoGluon 1.0.0 with best quality preset and TabPFN 0.1.9 with 32 ensemble members.
requirements.quote: AutoGluon 1.0.0 with the ”best quality” preset, and TabPFN 0.1.9 with 32 ensemble members (Hollmann et al., 2023).

requirements.stmt: Run HyperFast 0.1.3 without fine-tuning of the main networks but with 32 ensemble members.
requirements.quote: HyperFast 0.1.3 was used without fine-tuning of the main networks

requirements.stmt: Run experiments on 8 vCPU cores with 32 GiB memory.
requirements.quote: Each experiment was run on 8 vCPU cores with 32GiB memory on an internal cluster.
